accuracy.evidence: Tale facts checked: Anansi stories are Akan (Asante) from Ghana, including how Anansi bought the sky god Nyame's stories by capturing the python, leopard and hornets; Br'er Rabbit and the briar patch is an African American tale from the US South (published by Joel Chandler Harris, 1880), and both traditions have a sticky-doll tale (Anansi's gum doll, the tar baby); Theseus defeats the Minotaur in the labyrinth on Crete with Ariadne's thread; Momotarō travels to Onigashima with a dog, monkey and pheasant fed millet dumplings (kibi-dango); Yeh-Shen was recorded by Duan Chengshi around 850 with magic fish bones, a cave festival, golden shoes and a king; Rhodopis is told by Strabo, an eagle dropping her sandal in the king's lap at Memphis on the Nile; Perrault's Cendrillon (1697) has the fairy godmother, pumpkin coach, glass slipper and midnight; Midas (Ovid, Metamorphoses XI) turns even food to gold; Grimm's The Fisherman and His Wife ends with the wife back in her hovel.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the comparison errors teachers report for RL.4.9: judging characters by surface features instead of role (step 1 prediction, challenge tag animal), assuming one version's details are fixed or 'right' (step 2 prediction on the fairy godmother, challenge tags wrong and pattern, mastery m3), giving a theme as a single word or an event (theme step options tagged topic and event, mastery m7), choosing a message that fits only one tale (tag one), and listing similarities without differences (practice p4, mastery m4, challenge Q3).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtales works across cultures: tales from six lands are sorted into trickster, quest and Cinderella patterns, details are filed into the French or Chinese Cinderella, facts are placed in a three-zone Venn of Anansi and Br'er Rabbit, a theme is chosen that must fit two tales from different lands, and details are matched to the land they come from. flagmoral finds one fable's moral and flagtheme traces a theme within one text; neither compares versions or cultures, and the lab_distinct gate reports it under 30% similar to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Feedback carries the idea: filing Br'er Rabbit as a quest returns 'A small, clever character wins by tricking bigger ones: a trickster tale'; putting a fairy godmother under China says it is in the French version; placing 'gets stuck to a sticky doll' in only one ring explains both tales have one; choosing 'Greed.' says it is only a topic and a theme is a whole message; matching a Pharaoh to Japan prompts the learner to think which tale it comes from.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with a tempting wrong option: 'different animals from different lands cannot play the same part' (sorting places spider and rabbit in one pattern), and 'every Cinderella has a fairy godmother' (filing details shows magic fish bones in Yeh-Shen).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge items with tagged distractors and seven distinct messages: same animal versus same role, wrong land, topic or size instead of theme, one tale's event, a similarity when a difference was asked, calling a version wrong, and mistaking a changed detail for a different pattern.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the kid limit and the adult FK limit (the first adult draft read at grade 12.2 and was rewritten into shorter sentences). Kid paragraphs use pattern, trickster, quest and theme with one concrete pair each (Anansi and Br'er Rabbit, Midas and the fisherman's wife, the two Cinderellas).

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches (an adult phrase that tripped the 'the world of' filter was rewritten). Every step instruction is one task, and every item explanation names the tale detail that decides it.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px touch in light and dark for each step before and after Show me: tale cards wrap inside the drag card, Cinderella details and Venn facts stack without overlap (fixed after the first screenshots showed wrapped facts colliding; a measured stack helper now spaces them), the three theme options sit above the feedback box (the first layout put the third option under it and was fixed), and the five land boxes use two columns on phones.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: the three patterns, the two Cinderella versions, the three Venn zones, each theme option (with an aria-label 'Theme: …') and the five lands. The canvas aria-label reads the current card and feedback after each move, challenge feedback is an aria-live status, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
